speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin evaluating your painful leg ulcer, can you describe how long the lesion has been present and whether it appeared suddenly or gradually? Additionally, do you have any history of diabetes, venous insufficiency, or recent trauma to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and uveitis, does the ulcer have raised, violaceous borders, and is it extremely painful out of proportion to its size? Also, have you noticed any similar lesions on your trunk or arms, or have you experienced fever or joint pain recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a painful ulcer with violaceous borders following minor trauma, in the setting of Crohn's disease, is highly suggestive of pyoderma gangrenosum, though the signs of venous insufficiency are also notable. To confirm this and rule out infection, I need to see the lesion and check your inflammatory markers. REQUEST IMAGES. REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP, ESR, Wound Culture.
